A1_usd_reaction_underreaction.mechanism: Gold under-reacts to the dollar's response to US macro releases; it keeps moving opposite the USD surprise after the release window.

A2_gold_reaction_persistence.mechanism: Gold's own release-window move either continues (slow diffusion) or reverts (overshoot). Direction is a selected parameter, so the stability of its sign is what is tested.

A3_data_surprise_drift.mechanism: First-print surprises vs naive expectations (CPI/PCE core MoM vs prior, payrolls vs prior 2-month average, unemployment) are not fully priced on the day; hawkish surprises push gold down for days.

A4_gold_usd_divergence.mechanism: When gold fails to move opposite a USD release reaction, the macro-consistent move follows later.

A5_pre_fomc_drift.mechanism: Gold drifts up into scheduled FOMC statements (analogue of the equity pre-FOMC drift); long only, exit one hour before the statement.

A6_rates_dollar_leadlag.mechanism: Daily moves in real yields (FRED DFII10, used with a 1-business-day publication lag) or the dollar proxy lead gold by a day.

B1_cot_extremes_contrarian.mechanism: Crowded managed-money positioning (3-year COT index) mean-reverts.

B2_cot_mm_flow_momentum.mechanism: Speculative flow persists: the direction of managed-money net change predicts the next weeks.

B3_cot_hedger_flow.mechanism: Producers/merchants are informed hedgers: rising net hedger position (short covering) is bullish.

B4_oi_price_confirmation.mechanism: Price trends confirmed by rising open interest (new money) continue.

B6_tick_volume_imbalance_proxy.mechanism: PROXY ONLY: signed CFD tick-volume imbalance over 24 H1 bars (not exchange volume delta). Direction (follow/fade) is a selected parameter.

C1_regime_conditional.mechanism: Standard strategies work only in their natural regime: momentum in trending and in high volatility, mean reversion in ranging, breakouts after low volatility. Regime thresholds are fitted on train folds only; strategy parameters are fixed textbook values.
